summary.intent: Use idle time while ADR 0005 PR 2 finishes by delegating conflict-free parallel work to agents: a perf improvement, span-invariant tests on real repos, and a stop-word-aware name-matching prototype.
summary.outcome: Perf PR #103 was opened and linked to trail 362, with a reported 2.09 to 1.50 ratio to rg on stress/many and 1.86 to 1.56 on zod broad. A follow-up agent was asked to bump its changeset to minor. PR 2, the span-invariants test and the stop-word experiment are still running.

repo: The parse-depth bound used a 256 MiB stack thread spawned per file. On stress/many that cost 3.5 s of thread-summed CPU against 35 ms of parsing, and about 46% of profile samples were in `open`.
ADR 0004 bounds must stay untouched by perf work. Analysis threads now start once per search with the parse stack.
Rank scoring and sorting now run on rayon, which cut that step from 42 to 6 ms. Batch sizes are 64 files per thread for text search and 32 for analysis.
`rank_blocks` now requires `S: Sync`. That is a type-level breaking change, so the changeset must be minor rather than patch and carry a `**Breaking:**` note.
The repo's checks are `just test` (970 tests), fmt, typos, `just changesets` and rg-compare baseline scores. Clippy reports 6 existing lints, checked with `cargo clippy` directly.
`bench.py` was too noisy to trust and only ran zod and stress, because the other repos weren't cached. Interleaved medians as a ratio to rg were used instead.
PR #103 overlaps ADR 0005 PR 2 (batching and the sink), so a merge conflict is expected. Whichever lands second must merge main in.
workflow: Run non-conflicting work in parallel agents while a blocking PR finishes, and sequence work that shares the same code (for example the sink) after it.
Agent-reported benchmark numbers were not re-measured and the diff was not read, so they are unverified.
Push follow-up fixes without force, and merge main first if it has moved.

friction: bench.py was too noisy to use, and the other benchmark repos weren't cached.
#103 and ADR 0005 PR 2 touch overlapping batching and sink code, so a merge conflict is expected.
The initial changeset level was wrong, patch instead of minor, and needed a follow-up agent.
open_items: Review the #103 diff and re-measure its performance claims independently.
Second perf pass on the double `open` per file and the single-threaded directory walk (about 6%), after PR 2.
Merge main into whichever of #103 or PR 2 lands second.
Open PRs awaiting the user: #100, #101, #102, #103 and release PR #97.
Outcomes of the span-invariants test and the stop-word ranking prototype are still pending.
